description: SAHEL EARTHLAB is a team of young Nigerian innovators passionate about software engineering, AI, data science, and environmental sustainability. We develop technology-driven solutions to real-world challenges, including our project EarthScope 360. We welcome collaborators skilled in programming, GIS, climate science, data analysis, UI/UX design, research, and communication. Together, we aim to make a positive impact through innovation and teamwork.
summary: EarthScope 360 is an interactive web platform developed by SAHEL EARTHLAB to address the challenge of identifying and understanding Earth system trends. Using NASA POWER data, the platform enables users to explore temperature, rainfall, and relative humidity trends across Nigerian state capitals from 1981 to 2025. It processes environmental data, generates visual charts, and applies statistical analysis to identify patterns and changes over time. This project addresses the challenge by transforming complex climate datasets into accessible, understandable information. It is important because it promotes climate awareness, supports environmental education, and helps communities and decision-makers make better-informed decisions about environmental sustainability.

EARTHSCOPE 360 – PROJECT DETAILS

Project Name: EarthScope 360
Team Name: SAHEL EARTHLAB
Challenge: Be an Earth System Trend Detective!

1. What does the project do?

EarthScope 360 is an interactive web-based climate data analysis platform designed to help people explore and understand environmental changes across Nigeria. It uses historical NASA POWER data to analyse three important climate variables: temperature, precipitation (rainfall), and relative humidity. Users can select a Nigerian state capital, choose a climate variable, and specify a year range from 1981 to 2025. The platform generates visual charts and statistical analysis to help identify climate patterns and long-term trends.

2. How does it work?

EarthScope 360 works by allowing users to select a Nigerian state capital, choose a climate variable, and specify the period they want to investigate. The application retrieves the relevant historical climate data through the NASA POWER API. JavaScript processes the information, while Chart.js displays the results in interactive charts. The platform also applies linear regression and the Mann–Kendall statistical test to examine trends and changes over time. This makes it easier for users to understand climate information without manually processing large datasets.

3. What benefits does it have?

EarthScope 360 makes climate information more accessible and understandable. It helps users explore historical environmental patterns, improves climate awareness, supports environmental education, and provides useful information for students, researchers, and environmental organisations. It also transforms complex climate datasets into visual information that people can understand and use for research and informed decision-making.

4. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of EarthScope 360 is to improve climate awareness and promote the use of environmental data in Nigeria. By making historical climate information easier to access, analyse, and understand, the project aims to support climate research, environmental education, and informed decision-making. In the long term, it seeks to contribute to sustainable development by helping communities, researchers, and decision-makers better understand environmental changes.

5. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop the project?

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML was used to structure the website, CSS to design its appearance, and JavaScript to handle data retrieval, processing, and analysis. NASA POWER API was used as the source of historical climate data, while Chart.js was used to create visual charts. GitHub was used for source-code management, and GitHub Pages was used to host the website. A laptop, code editor, and web browser were used during development and testing. The application requires an internet connection to retrieve climate data.

6. How did the project get created?

EarthScope 360 was developed by SAHEL EARTHLAB in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our team first examined the challenge and identified the need for a simple way to explore and understand historical Earth system trends. We selected Nigeria as our initial focus and identified temperature, precipitation, and relative humidity as the major climate variables to analyse. We researched the NASA POWER data service and developed a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We integrated the NASA POWER API to retrieve historical climate data, implemented statistical analysis to examine trends, and used Chart.js to present the results visually. We also expanded the location selector to cover all 36 Nigerian states and the Federal Capital Territory. Finally, we tested the application and published it online through GitHub Pages.

7. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered data reliability, accessibility, local relevance, usability, and technical limitations. We selected NASA POWER as our climate data source and focused on Nigerian state capitals to make the platform relevant to local users. We considered three important climate variables: temperature, precipitation, and relative humidity. We also considered historical data availability from 1981 to 2025, the need for simple visual presentations, and the importance of statistical methods for identifying trends. Additionally, we considered internet connectivity and the limitations of gridded climate estimates compared with direct weather-station measurements. We designed the project with future improvements and expansion in mind.
